memory_candidates.content: In Lean 4/Mathlib, the Finset literal sugar `{a, b, c}` does NOT desugar uniformly to nested `insert`: its trailing element is built via the `Singleton` typeclass instance, not `insert _ ∅`. If a downstream elimination API only provides simp lemmas for `insert` and `∅` (e.g. `SchemaUnion.insert_iff : SchemaUnion (insert t S) φ ↔ t.Holds φ ∨ SchemaUnion S φ` and `SchemaUnion.empty_iff : SchemaUnion ∅ φ ↔ False`), a Finset built with `{a,b,c}` sugar will unfold partway and then get stuck on the trailing singleton term, producing a confusing `subst`/type-mismatch error rather than a clean 'lemma not found'. Fix: define the Finset via explicit nested `insert a (insert b (insert c ∅))` when its elements need to fully unfold through an insert/empty-only simp set.

When proving N structurally-similar `SchemaUnion sysTags φ ↔ <Sys>Axiom φ`-style bridge lemmas across systems with varying differentiator-tag counts (1, 2, or 3 extra tags unioned with a shared core), the `rcases`/`rintro` pattern that destructures the simp-unfolded disjunction needs EXACTLY `(differentiator count) + (core size)` comma-separated sub-patterns in the precise nesting order (outermost insert first), each with the right existential arity. Undercounting by even one slot silently drops a middle tag from the pattern and desyncs every subsequent arity, surfacing many slots later as a confusing `subst: invalid equality proof` error rather than a slot-count error at the dropped position. Mitigation: before writing the rcases line for a new differentiator-count shape, explicitly enumerate the tag order and arity list (e.g. as a numbered comment) rather than eyeballing it; once correct for one system of a given shape, the same slot-count pattern reliably transfers to every other system sharing that shape.

For a family of `<Sys>Axiom` inductives that are each provably equivalent to `SchemaUnion sysTags`, the bridge equivalence's two directions want DIFFERENT proof strategies for best ergonomics: forward (SchemaUnion -> inductive) benefits from simp-unfolding the union via an insert/empty elimination API into a named disjunction, then closing each resulting goal with `all_goals first | exact Ctor1 _ … | exact Ctor2 _ … | …` (arity mismatches make `exact` fail cleanly, so goal order need not match the `first` list order); backward (inductive -> SchemaUnion) is simpler as a direct anonymous-constructor witness `cases h with | ctor args => exact ⟨.tag, by decide, args…, rfl⟩` with no simp needed at all, since you already know exactly which tag and witness to supply once you've cased on the constructor.
